subject: [Escalation] Checkoutly live checkout failures - SDK heartbeat split
messages:
From: Natalie Chen <natalie@checkoutly.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production outage: spike in p99 and 502s from live checkout

Hi Vivek,

We started seeing large spikes in latency (p99 > 6s) and intermittent 502s on our live checkout between 02:50-03:30 PST this morning. Errors correlate with streaming responses timing out — the client shows repeated stream reconnects and aborted requests.

Attached are trimmed logs and a sample request id (req_8a3f2b). The problem began after our customers received the auto-update to Checkoutly web client 2.1.4 last night.

Can Redwood triage immediately? This is impacting multiple large merchants (one flagged our SLA team).

Attachments: ops-sample-logs.txt (100KB excerpt)

—
Natalie Chen
Head of Integrations, Checkoutly
natalie@checkoutly.com
+1 415-555-0198

Cc: support@checkoutly.com
Date: 2027-05-09T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production outage: spike in p99 and 502s from live checkout (urgent)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production outage: spike in p99 and 502s from live checkout (urgent)

Quick triage notes (prelim):
- Root symptom: streaming parser on our edge rejects frames where the "heartbeat" control frame is split across TCP segments (partial header seen, parser treats as malformed and closes connection).
- Correlation: spike starts after client 2.1.4 rollout which introduced an "aggressive coalescing" change that sends the heartbeat flag in a separate small frame under certain Node versions.
- Impact: increased stream reconnects -> token replays -> inventory/checkout race -> 502s + p99 blowups.

Immediate ask: roll back the coalescing change in client 2.1.4 (Checkoutly) and push a temporary config on our side to tolerate split headers for their traffic. I can assemble a canary patch for our runtime to accept split-heartbeat sequences within the hour.

Attaching a short checklist for a controlled canary and rollback.

—
Marissa Cole
TPM, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production outage: spike in p99 and 502s from live checkout (metrics & next steps)

Adding metrics and next steps:
- Error rate on the Checkoutly tenant jumped from baseline 0.12% -> 3.4% in a 30m window starting 02:48 PST. Throughput dropped ~18% as retries pile up.
- Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/metrics/checkoutly?from=2027-05-09T02:30Z (internal)
- Suggested immediate mitigations:
  1) Toggle off "chunked header reassembly optimization" for Checkoutly at ingress (will add ~0.6ms median cost but restore correctness).
  2) Canary runtime change to accept split heartbeat frames for 10% of requests.
  3) Coordinate with Checkoutly to roll their client to 2.1.3 (canary) while we monitor.

I'll open JIRA INF-4729 and prepare an incident email for execs. We should also prepare an SLA credit estimate for Natalie.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production outage: spike in p99 and 502s from live checkout (mitigation plan)

Plan of action (ops):
- Step 1 (15m): Apply ingress toggle for Checkoutly tenant to disable header coalescing optimization. Ops runbook: /runbooks/ingress-header-fix-v2 (internal).
- Step 2 (30m): Roll runtime canary that relaxes streaming parser to accept split-heartbeat (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% if green).
- Step 3 (2h): Coordinate with Checkoutly to rollback client 2.1.4 -> 2.1.3 and push node-specific patch.

I've created JIRA INF-4729 and a short Doc (link in related_links). I'll own rollout and status updates to the customer. Please loop Legal if SLA credit asked.

Attachments: playbook-rollout-checklist.pdf

—
Sean Gallagher
Head of Incident Response
Redwood Inference

From: Natalie Chen <natalie@checkoutly.com>

Date: 2027-05-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production outage: spike in p99 and 502s from live checkout (customer impact)

Thank you — appreciate the rapid response. Two asks from my side:
1) ETA for the first mitigation (ingress toggle + canary) and estimated time to full recovery? Our ops team is pushing customers to stall traffic until we have a confirmed fix.
2) Can Redwood produce a Node-specific temp patch we can distribute while we rollback the web client? Our Node hosts are the ones most affected.

Also escalating request for SLA credits from one of our largest merchants — copying SLA team. We'll need the incident report to process the credit.

—
Natalie Chen
Head of Integrations, Checkoutly

Subject: Re: Production outage: spike in p99 and 502s from live checkout (customer impact)

Natalie — thanks for the clear asks. Status update:
- ETA: ingress toggle + initial canary applied within 45 minutes; full rollout projected ~6 hours if canary metrics look stable.
- Node patch: we've prepared a minimal Node SDK shim that forces coalescing to the previous behavior (attached: node_sdk_patch.diff). It ships as a hot patch you can apply to affected hosts.
- SLA: we'll provide a formal incident report and a preliminary credit estimate by EOD. Legal and billing are looped for the credit calculation.

I'll host a brief exec call at 4:00pm PT to walk through timeline and impacts (invite forthcoming).

Attachments: node_sdk_patch.diff

Vivek Kulkarni
